hook: A camera rode a shuttle booster to 2,900 mph and back.
narration: This camera rode a space shuttle booster to about twenty-nine hundred miles an hour.
It was mounted on one of the two solid rocket boosters, looking up at the shuttle.
Liftoff. Then the readout climbed past two thousand miles an hour.
Then the boosters burned out and broke away.
Small separation motors fire to push each spent booster clear of the shuttle, so the two never collide.
It kept coasting up to forty-one miles, with the Earth curving below.
Then it fell back toward the ocean, tumbling.
outcome: And the booster splashed down in the ocean, about four hundred seconds after liftoff.
title: Riding a shuttle booster to 2,900 mph
question_comment: Would you ride a booster up and back down if you could?

description:
Cameras mounted on the space shuttle's solid rocket boosters rode them up through separation and back down to splashdown, in footage NASA compiled from shuttle flights STS-117 and STS-127.
